steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Thermoplastics: linear polymer chains - soften when heated, solidify when cooled, can be remelted repeatedly. ABS (lego), acrylic (signs), PP (living hinges), HDPE (milk bottles). | Key Fact: Thermosets: cross-linked polymer chains - set permanently once cured, cannot be remelted, char when reheated. Epoxy resin (adhesives), melamine (worktops), polyester resin (fibreglass). | Key Fact: Polypropylene (PP): excellent fatigue resistance (living hinges on bottle caps), chemical resistant, lightweight, microwave-safe. | Key Fact: Polycarbonate: virtually unbreakable, transparent, high impact resistance - safety glasses, riot shields, CDs.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Explain the structural difference between thermoplastics and thermosets and how this affects their recyclability. | A designer needs a transparent, impact-resistant material for a safety goggles lens. Justify the choice of polycarbonate over acrylic. | Explain why a living hinge on a shampoo bottle cap must be made from polypropylene and not from acrylic.
